findings.evidence: Uniqueness.lean:110-119 uses `heq` only at `t = 0` and via `heq.mono Ioi_subset_Ici_self`; `Basic.lean:248-250` proves `ContinuousOn (bernsteinLevyJumpExponent μ) (Ici 0)` from `integrable_min_one` alone; `Set.EqOn.of_subset_closure` exists in Mathlib (`Mathlib/Topology/Separation/Hausdorff.lean:504`, applied at `Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/PhragmenLindelof.lean:768`).
findings.fix: State the hypothesis on `Ioi 0`; recover `a = a'` from `Set.EqOn.of_subset_closure` with `closure_Ioi 0 = Ici 0`, which needs `continuousOn_bernsteinLevyJumpExponent` (currently `private` at `Basic.lean:248`) made public, in line with this PR's other promotions. Callers with `EqOn … (Ici 0)`, including `existsUnique_eqOn_bernsteinLevyKhintchineExponent` at line 157, pass `.mono Ioi_subset_Ici_self`.
findings.issue: `heq : EqOn … (Ici 0)` is stronger than the proof needs: the only use of the point `0` is line 111 (`heq (mem_Ici.mpr le_rfl)`) to get `a = a'`, but both exponents are continuous on `Ici 0`, so agreement on `Ioi 0` already forces the endpoint value. As stated, the theorem cannot be applied to triplets known to agree only on the open half-line — the setting this file's own `OpenHalfLine` import serves.

findings.evidence: Each body reduces to `integrable_exp_neg_mul_bernsteinLevyDerivativeMeasure hμ.integrable_min_one ht` (line 64) or its consequences; no occurrence of `measure_singleton_zero` in lines 55-93. `Basic.lean` states exactly these facts under the weaker hypothesis (`integrable_exp_neg_mul_bernsteinLevyDerivativeMeasure`, line 228; `..._of_integrable_min_one` variants at lines 337, 359).
findings.fix: Change the hypothesis in all four to `hμ : Integrable (fun x : ℝ≥0 => min 1 (x : ℝ)) μ` and pass `hμ.integrable_min_one` at the two call sites in `eq_of_eqOn_bernsteinLevyKhintchineExponent`.
findings.issue: Same class of defect: `integrable_exp_neg_mul_jumpDerivativeMeasure` (line 60), `integrable_exp_neg_mul_bernsteinLevyKhintchineDerivativeMeasure` (66), `laplaceTransform_bernsteinLevyKhintchineDerivativeMeasure` (73) and `representsLaplaceOnIoi_bernsteinLevyKhintchineDerivativeMeasure` (86) all take `hμ : IsBernsteinLevyMeasure μ` but use only `hμ.integrable_min_one`; the `μ {0} = 0` clause is unused, contradicting the file-neighbour convention.

summary: The uniqueness theorem assumes agreement on `Ici 0` where agreement on `Ioi 0` suffices (the value at `0` is forced by continuity at the endpoint), and four private helpers carry `IsBernsteinLevyMeasure` where only integrability of `min 1 x` is used. Otherwise the statements sit at the natural level.
